title: Trail and Provision
premise: When a flood deposits a sealed chest bearing the crest of Vessia—a drowned nation erased from maps a century ago—riverboat captain Yara Whitlock discovers her late father was its courier, and that the chest's contents can either restore Vessia's exiled heirs or arm the corrupt consortium that destroyed it. Hunted by consortium agents and shadowed by a charming archivist who may be heir or traitor, Yara pilots her boat upstream toward Vessia's hidden source valley, where a treaty hidden in the chest could break the consortium's dam monopoly. Betrayals strip her of crew, boat, and certainty, forcing her to choose between loyalty to her father's memory and the truth of what he actually did. At the source, she exposes the archivist's deception, delivers the treaty to the surviving heirs, and chooses to burn her father's confession rather than let it poison the future—returning downstream with the river, and herself, freed.
about_author: Xanthe Sandoval is a former river guide who spent a decade charting waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. Her novels blend nautical authenticity with political intrigue, earning her a devoted readership among adventure readers.

chapters.title: What the Flood Brings
chapters.summary: Yara, piloting her aging riverboat the Meridian through spring floodwaters, nets a waterlogged chest stamped with the seal of Vessia, a nation she's only heard of in barroom songs. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: restless curiosity curdling into unease when she finds her father's handwriting inside the lid.

chapters.title: Her Father's Ink
chapters.summary: Examining the chest at dock, Yara finds documents her father, dead five years, was paid to courier—plus a half-burned letter warning that the contents must reach 'the source or no one.' A stranger in a gray coat watches her boat. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief reopened, the past refusing to stay sunk.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Elias Vane, a self-described Vessian archivist, offers Yara passage money to carry him upstream to the source valley. He knows too much about the chest and too little about the river. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: wary bargain struck; she trusts her river, not him.

chapters.title: Passengers and Predators
chapters.summary: The Meridian departs with Elias and two paying passengers—one of whom, a quiet woman named Sef, carries a consortium mark tattooed inside her wrist. Consortium agents raid a downstream dock asking about a chest. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the hunt has begun, and her boat is the quarry.

chapters.title: The Drowned Nation's Map
chapters.summary: Elias shows Yara the chest's prize: a treaty granting Vessian heirs rights to the river's source, voiding the consortium's dam claims. He reveals the consortium drowned Vessia deliberately. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: his zealotry is real—but he's editing something out.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Yara's first mate, Doss, is caught selling their route to consortium agents and marooned on a sandbar. The crew's loyalty fractures; Sef quietly proves her worth during the confrontation. POV: Doss. Emotional beat: betrayal from inside the family she built.

chapters.title: The Lock at Karst Reach
chapters.summary: The consortium controls the Karst Reach locks and demands the chest as toll. Yara runs her boat through the flooded side-channel instead, a passage only she knows, nearly losing the Meridian. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror; her river knowledge is her only armor.

chapters.title: Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef admits she was consortium surveillance, sent to track the chest—but defected after seeing what the consortium did to source villages. Yara must decide whether to throw her off or trust her. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: the cost of switching sides, and Yara's first real act of trust.

chapters.title: The Hanging Town
chapters.summary: In a river town under consortium occupation, they witness a public execution of Vessian sympathizers. Elias wants to intervene; Yara drags him away, and the argument cracks their fragile alliance. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: the difference between witnessing and surviving.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Deciphering the chest's second layer, Yara finds her father's ledger proving he took consortium money for years—couriering for both sides. The father of her memory begins to dissolve. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead colliding with the truth about them.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Nine Sisters
chapters.summary: A consortium gunboat forces the Meridian into the unmapped Nine Sisters rapids. Sef is thrown overboard; Yara's impossible piloting saves her, but the boat's hull is cracked. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: survival bought at the edge of ruin, and a bond sealed in white water.

chapters.title: The Healer of Vell Hollow
chapters.summary: Holed up in a hidden Vessian village while the Meridian is patched, they meet an old woman who recognizes the treaty—and reveals the heir it names is alive. Elias reacts strangely. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: hope with a hairline fracture running through it.

chapters.title: What Elias Carries
chapters.summary: Sef catches Elias burning pages from the treaty's annex. He confesses partially: the named heir is not who the exiles believe, and revealing it will shatter the restoration movement. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: a true believer protecting a lie he thinks is kinder.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Offer
chapters.summary: Consortium director Halvard Crane intercepts them with an offer: the Meridian freed, her crew pardoned, a fortune—if Yara surrenders the chest. He shows her proof her father died working for him. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: temptation wearing her father's face.

chapters.title: Mutiny at Anchor
chapters.summary: Half the crew, terrified and bribed, moves to seize the chest for Crane. Yara and Sef hold the deck through a violent standoff; the mutineers are set ashore with fair shares. POV: Doss, returned and repentant, tipping the balance. Emotional beat: leadership means choosing who leaves.

chapters.title: The Last Tributary
chapters.summary: Beyond consortium charts, the river narrows to unmapped gorge water. The Meridian is abandoned at the gorge mouth; the final leg is on foot with the chest, pursued by Crane's men. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: leaving her boat behind is leaving her old self behind.

chapters.title: The Source Valley
chapters.summary: They reach the hidden valley: Vessia's survivors, a functioning exile nation the consortium never found. But the elders' claim rests on the treaty—and Elias's secret is about to break it open. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: arrival that feels like a verdict delayed.

chapters.title: The True Heir
chapters.summary: Elias reveals the truth before Crane's arriving force can use it: the rightful heir is Sef, the defected spy, not the exile figurehead the elders anointed. The valley splits. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: an identity she fled becoming the only thing that can save everyone.

chapters.title: Crane at the Gates
chapters.summary: Crane's mercenaries breach the valley, demanding the treaty and the heir. Yara uses the gorge's flood season—her river knowledge, transposed to land—springing a trap that turns the valley's waterworks against the attackers. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the captain's craft, weaponized at last.

chapters.title: Her Father's Confession
chapters.summary: Among Crane's captured papers, Yara finds her father's full confession: he betrayed Vessia's location decades ago, then spent his life couriering restitution. The chest was his penance. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: she can love the man and condemn the act—and must choose which to carry forward.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: With the treaty signed and Sef acknowledged, the elders want the confession read publicly to justify reprisals. Yara burns it before the assembly, arguing the future cannot be built on inherited guilt. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: her costliest act of mercy, and her freest.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: The Meridian, repaired by Vessian hands, carries Yara and a small new crew back downriver as the consortium's dam monopoly begins to crack. She passes the sandbar where it all started and doesn't stop. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: homecoming without returning—measuring life, at last, in something other than miles.
